sentences.en: The Great Salt Lake in Utah is drying up, creating a bowl of toxic dust that threatens to poison the air in one of the nation's fastest-growing metro areas.
sentences.zh: 犹他州的大盐湖正在干涸，形成了一个有毒的尘埃盆地，威胁着要毒害该国增长最快的大都市区之一的空气。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Christopher Flavel on the struggle to avert that catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事克里斯托弗·弗拉维尔将讲述如何避免这场灾难的斗争。

sentences.en: It's Friday, July 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月22日，星期五。

sentences.en: So Chris, you cover climate for The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，你负责《纽约时报》的气候报道。

sentences.en: Tell me why you decided to go to Utah.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你为什么决定去犹他州。

sentences.en: So at the beginning of the year, I started hearing stories about what's happening with the Great Salt Lake and, in particular, this fear that it was beginning to dry up.
sentences.zh: 今年年初，我开始听到关于大盐湖现状的故事，特别是人们担心它开始干涸了。

sentences.en: Our top story this morning, the levels of the Great Salt Lake have tied the record low that was set back in 1963.
sentences.zh: 今天早上我们的头条新闻是，大盐湖的水位已经追平了1963年创下的历史最低纪录。

sentences.en: They hit a record low last summer.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，水位就达到了历史最低点。

sentences.en: This week, the Great Salt Lake has been flirting with historic low levels.
sentences.zh: 本周，大盐湖一直徘徊在历史最低水位附近。

sentences.en: Which caused everyone to suddenly sit up and pay attention.
sentences.zh: 这让所有人都突然警觉起来，开始关注这件事。

sentences.en: Utah Governor Spencer Cox has now declared a state of emergency and called on the people of Utah to reduce their water use and pray for rain.
sentences.zh: 犹他州州长斯宾塞·考克斯现已宣布进入紧急状态，并呼吁犹他州人民减少用水，祈求降雨。

sentences.en: And start to ask themselves, wait, what would actually happen if this lake disappeared?
sentences.zh: 并开始问自己，等等，如果这个湖消失了，到底会发生什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so let's start with the lake itself.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们先从湖本身说起。

sentences.en: When you say the name, I think Utah because of Salt Lake City.
sentences.zh: 提到这个名字，因为盐湖城的关系，我会想到犹他州。

sentences.en: But otherwise, I'm not sure I know very much about this lake.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，我不确定我对这个湖了解多少。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Covering 1,700 square miles, it's the largest American lake west of the Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 它占地1700平方英里，是密西西比河以西最大的美国湖泊。

sentences.en: Picture a gargantuan body of water that really defines the northern half of Utah.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，一个巨大的水体，它真正定义了犹他州的北半部。

sentences.en: What makes Great Salt Lake so unique is that its water is up to five times saltier than the ocean.
sentences.zh: 大盐湖之所以如此独特，是因为它的水盐度比海洋高出五倍。

sentences.en: It is, as the name suggests, heavily salty.
sentences.zh: 正如其名，它盐分极高。

sentences.en: The eastern shore of Great Salt Lake is America's Serengeti for migratory birds.
sentences.zh: 大盐湖的东岸是美国候鸟的塞伦盖蒂大草原。

sentences.en: So, birds that are flying across the continent stop here for food.
sentences.zh: 所以，飞越大陆的鸟类会在这里停留觅食。

sentences.en: This lake is not just a landmark, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这个湖不仅仅是一个地标。

sentences.en: It is a linchpin for our ecology, the ecology of a region where most Utahns live.
sentences.zh: 它是我们生态系统的关键，也是大多数犹他州人居住地区的生态核心。

sentences.en: Crucial part of the landscape in terms of weather patterns.
sentences.zh: 它是天气模式中至关重要的一部分。

sentences.en: It protects us from dust storMs. It helps our snowpack.
sentences.zh: 它保护我们免受沙尘暴的侵袭。它有助于我们的积雪。

sentences.en: It helps increase precipitation and snowfall in the mountains, which increases water supply for those that live there.
sentences.zh: 它有助于增加山区的降水和降雪，从而增加了当地居民的供水。

sentences.en: And it also powers over a billion dollars of Utah's economy.
sentences.zh: 它还为犹他州的经济贡献了超过十亿美元的产值。

sentences.en: And it's an important part of sort of the psyche and the identity of Salt Lake City and Utah.
sentences.zh: 它也是盐湖城和犹他州心理和身份认同的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: So, it would be hard to overstate just how important this lake is for a lot of reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论怎么强调这个湖的重要性都不为过，原因有很多。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, you said there was a fear that the lake might actually dry up completely.
sentences.zh: 你说过有人担心这个湖可能会彻底干涸。

sentences.en: So, what would happen if the lake did actually dry up?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果湖真的干涸了会发生什么？

sentences.en: You know, one of the state lawmakers I met with, who's a Republican, said it would be like an environmental nuclear bomb going off if this lake disappeared.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我遇到的一位共和党州议员说，如果这个湖消失了，就像引爆了一颗环境核弹。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, I realized I had to see the lake for myself and also get a better idea of what's causing it to shrink and what people are doing about it, trying to save it.
sentences.zh: 所以我意识到我必须亲自去看看这个湖，并更好地了解是什么导致它萎缩，以及人们正在采取什么措施来拯救它。

sentences.en: So, one of the first things I did when I landed in Salt Lake City was I drove out to the lake.
sentences.zh: 所以，我到达盐湖城后做的第一件事就是开车去湖边。

sentences.en: But even before you see anything else, something looks wrong, right?
sentences.zh: 但在你看到其他任何东西之前，有些事情看起来就不对劲，对吧？

sentences.en: You're looking out on the side of the causeway and you see these vast expanses of dry land.
sentences.zh: 你看着堤道的一侧，看到大片大片的干涸土地。

sentences.en: And it's a kind of dry land that doesn't really fit any framework that I had.
sentences.zh: 那种干涸的土地并不符合我脑海中的任何框架。

sentences.en: It's not soil.
sentences.zh: 它不是土壤。

sentences.en: It's not sand.
sentences.zh: 它不是沙子。

sentences.en: There's clearly no vegetation.
sentences.zh: 显然没有植被。

sentences.en: It just looks wrong.
sentences.zh: 看起来就是不对劲。

sentences.en: So, I drive past these empty expanses and meet Kevin Perry.
sentences.zh: 于是，我开车经过这些空旷的区域，见到了凯文·佩里。

sentences.en: If we go a little bit further south, we can get a really nice perspective of what used to be lake, which is completely dry.
sentences.zh: 如果我们再往南走一点，就能很好地看到曾经是湖泊的地方，现在已经完全干涸了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A professor of atmospheric sciences at the University of Utah.
sentences.zh: 他是犹他大学的大气科学教授。

sentences.en: And what did he tell you?
sentences.zh: 他跟你说了什么？

sentences.en: He described two big challenges that are causing the lake to shrink.
sentences.zh: 他描述了导致湖泊萎缩的两个巨大挑战。

sentences.en: It's mostly due to the fact that we divert too much water for other purposes.
sentences.zh: 这主要是因为我们将太多的水用于其他目的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The first is how much water humans are pulling from rivers and streams before that water gets to the lake.
sentences.zh: 首先是人类在水到达湖泊之前从河流和溪流中抽取了多少水。

sentences.en: The water that's being diverted, what's it being diverted for?
sentences.zh: 被分流的水，是用来做什么的？

sentences.en: 70% of it's being diverted for agriculture.
sentences.zh: 其中70%用于农业。

sentences.en: You know, 15% for cities and 15% for industry.
sentences.zh: 你知道，15%用于城市，15%用于工业。

sentences.en: So, think of the watershed around the Great Salt Lake as sort of a perfect miniature system.
sentences.zh: 所以，把大盐湖周围的流域想象成一个完美的微型系统。

sentences.en: You've got precipitation falling in the mountains above Salt Lake City as snow.
sentences.zh: 盐湖城上方的山区以降雪的形式降水。

sentences.en: And that snow melts, feeding rivers and streaMs.
sentences.zh: 雪融化后，汇入河流和溪流。

sentences.en: And eventually, those rivers and streams empty into the Great Salt Lake.
sentences.zh: 最终，这些河流和溪流汇入大盐湖。

sentences.en: But along the way, you've got people diverting that water with a massive amount going to agriculture.
sentences.zh: 但在沿途，人们在分流这些水，其中大部分流向了农业。

sentences.en: And what's changing now is you're seeing a huge population boom in Salt Lake City that's making things worse, pulling even more water away from the lake.
sentences.zh: 而现在发生的变化是，盐湖城的人口激增，这让情况变得更糟，从湖中抽取了更多的水。

sentences.en: It's one of the fastest growing areas in the country.
sentences.zh: 这是全国增长最快的地区之一。

sentences.en: And when you're there, you can feel it.
sentences.zh: 当你身处其中时，你能感觉到。

sentences.en: You can see new subdivisions sprouting all the time at the edge of the metropolis.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到大都市边缘不断涌现新的住宅区。

sentences.en: It's almost literally getting bigger as you watch it.
sentences.zh: 当你看着它时，它几乎在字面上变得越来越大。

sentences.en: So, as more people come to Salt Lake City, and a lot are coming, this diversion problem gets worse.
sentences.zh: 所以，随着越来越多的人来到盐湖城，而且来的人很多，这种分流问题就变得更严重了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: But even as that's happening, you've got a separate challenge, an interlocking set of problems related to climate change.
sentences.zh: 但即使在这种情况发生的同时，你还面临着另一个挑战，即与气候变化相关的一系列相互交织的问题。

sentences.en: The western United States is facing a severe drought.
sentences.zh: 美国西部正面临严重的干旱。

sentences.en: And that's really shorthand for two things.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是两件事的缩写。

sentences.en: One is less precipitation, which means less snowpack forming in the first place.
sentences.zh: 一是降水减少，这意味着积雪本身形成的就少了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, we're having a fairly poor snowpack this year.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们今年的积雪相当少。

sentences.en: We're like 80% of normal.
sentences.zh: 我们只有正常水平的80%左右。

sentences.en: So, if we were at 100% of normal on snowpack, we divert so much water that the lake would still shrink another foot next year.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使我们的积雪达到正常水平的100%，我们分流了太多的水，明年湖泊水位仍会下降一英尺。

sentences.en: And the other one is heat.
sentences.zh: 另一个是高温。

sentences.en: Higher temperatures mean that even if the snowpack does form, you've got more of that snow evaporating due to high heat.
sentences.zh: 更高的温度意味着即使积雪形成了，由于高温，更多的雪也会蒸发掉。

sentences.en: Well, last year, the spring runoff, we got six inches of water in the lake.
sentences.zh: 嗯，去年春季径流，我们湖里只得到了六英寸的水。

sentences.en: And we still lost two feet.
sentences.zh: 但我们还是损失了两英尺。

sentences.en: So, we went down a foot and a half last year.
sentences.zh: 所以去年水位下降了一英尺半。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, it's not just less precipitation.
sentences.zh: 所以，不仅仅是降水减少了。

sentences.en: It's that once the snow falls, more of it is being lost back into the air, and less of it is entering these tributaries to begin with.
sentences.zh: 而是雪一旦落下，更多的雪又蒸发回空气中，而流入这些支流的水本来就少了。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, it basically evaporates as opposed to turning into water and flowing into the lake.
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上是蒸发了，而不是变成水流入湖中。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, between population growth, drought, and rising temperatures, this lake is really facing a crisis.
sentences.zh: 所以，在人口增长、干旱和气温上升的共同作用下，这个湖确实面临着危机。

sentences.en: So, Chris, how much longer do we expect the Great Salt Lake to actually exist?
sentences.zh: 那么，克里斯，我们预计大盐湖还能存在多久？

sentences.en: The short answer, and the reason this is so scary, is no one really knows how long we might have left until this lake disappears.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答，也是这件事如此可怕的原因，是没人真正知道这个湖消失前我们还有多少时间。

sentences.en: But the better question, and maybe the scarier question, is how long until the negative effects of that lake shrinking start to be felt?
sentences.zh: 但更好的问题，也许是更可怕的问题，是距离感受到湖泊萎缩带来的负面影响还有多久？

sentences.en: And on that point, the really scary answer is they might have started already.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，真正可怕的答案是，它们可能已经开始了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about those effects.
sentences.zh: 那我们来谈谈这些影响。

sentences.en: Walk me through what's happening.
sentences.zh: 带我了解一下正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Well, let's start with the economic consequences.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们先从经济后果说起。

sentences.en: One of the reasons that this lake is so important is it helps increase the amount of snow that falls in the ski resorts above Salt Lake City.
sentences.zh: 这个湖之所以如此重要，原因之一是它有助于增加盐湖城上方滑雪胜地的降雪量。

sentences.en: The snow that we get in October, November, December would be primarily lake-effects snow, and that's what you need to jumpstart your season.
sentences.zh: 我们在十月、十一月、十二月得到的雪主要是湖泊效应雪，这是你启动滑雪季所需要的。

sentences.en: Really, really great ski resorts that are a big tourism driver for the local economy.
sentences.zh: 非常非常棒的滑雪胜地，是当地经济的重要旅游驱动力。

sentences.en: Not only that, but as the lake shrinks, it hurts the mineral extraction industries.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，随着湖泊萎缩，它还损害了矿产开采行业。

sentences.en: But it's the only source of magnesium metal for the United States.
sentences.zh: 它是美国唯一的金属镁来源。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you've got a lot of money in Utah coming from companies that can use this water to extract minerals like magnesium from it.
sentences.zh: 所以，犹他州有大量资金来自那些利用湖水从中提取镁等矿物质的公司。

sentences.en: So, as the lake shrinks, that starts to go away.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着湖泊萎缩，这些收入就开始消失了。

sentences.en: The second one is the ecological consequences.
sentences.zh: 第二个是生态后果。

sentences.en: The Great Salt Lake is a massively important stopover.
sentences.zh: 大盐湖是一个极其重要的中转站。

sentences.en: You hear the number of 10 million migratory birds stopping here.
sentences.zh: 你听过有1000万只候鸟在这里停留的数字。

sentences.en: The base of the food chain is the brine flies and the brine shrimp.
sentences.zh: 食物链的基础是卤虫和卤虫虾。

sentences.en: They all congregate at this lake because it's a source of food.
sentences.zh: 它们都聚集在这个湖里，因为这里是食物来源。

sentences.en: And when the lake hits 19% salinity, then the brine shrimp have to spend so much energy expelling salt that they can no longer reproduce.
sentences.zh: 当湖泊盐度达到19%时，卤虫虾就必须消耗大量能量来排出盐分，以至于它们无法再繁殖。

sentences.en: And at that point, the food chain collapses.
sentences.zh: 到那时，食物链就会崩溃。

sentences.en: Kevin Perry said 19%, but a different expert I spoke with said that number could be as low as 17% salt content.
sentences.zh: 凯文·佩里说是19%，但我交谈过的另一位专家说，这个数字可能低至17%的含盐量。

sentences.en: And the lake is expected to hit that number this summer, right now.
sentences.zh: 而且预计这个夏天，也就是现在，湖泊就会达到这个数字。

sentences.en: So, what you're saying, Chris, is that there are a lot of fates tied to this lake.
sentences.zh: 所以，克里斯，你的意思是，有很多命运与这个湖息息相关。

sentences.en: I mean, there's the fate of agriculture, the mining industry, and tourism, and the fate of the environment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有农业、采矿业和旅游业的命运，还有环境的命运。

sentences.en: Exactly, but we haven't gotten to the worst part yet.
sentences.zh: 没错，但我们还没说到最糟糕的部分。

sentences.en: It's also the people who breathe the air around the Great Salt Lake because what is trapped in the earth underneath this lake is very hazardous heavy metals.
sentences.zh: 还有呼吸大盐湖周围空气的人们，因为困在大盐湖下方土壤中的是极其危险的重金属。

sentences.en: I'm talking about things like arsenic, antimony, copper, zirconium, things that you do not want in your body and that you do not want in your lungs.
sentences.zh: 我说的是砷、锑、铜、锆之类的东西，这些东西你不想让它们进入你的身体，也不想让它们进入你的肺部。

sentences.en: And as the lake disappears, those metals and the soil they're trapped in become exposed.
sentences.zh: 随着湖泊消失，这些金属以及它们所困的土壤就会暴露出来。

sentences.en: And then once you get dust storms and wind, pulling that soil, that dirt off the exposed
sentences.zh: 然后一旦出现沙尘暴和风，就会把这些土壤、尘土从暴露的

sentences.en: lake bed, moving it into the air, and eventually into the lung tissue of people who live in Salt
sentences.zh: 湖床上卷起，带入空气中，最终进入居住在盐

sentences.en: Lake City.
sentences.zh: 湖城的人们的肺组织中。

sentences.en: And that could be the most serious concern and serious consequence as the lake dries up.
sentences.zh: 随着湖泊干涸，这可能是最严重的担忧和后果。

sentences.en: Can people die from inhaling it?
sentences.zh: 人们会因为吸入这些东西而死亡吗？

sentences.en: I mean, how dangerous is it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它有多危险？

sentences.en: Yeah, so there's two specific threats that are different, but both worrisome.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以有两个具体的威胁，虽然不同，但都令人担忧。

sentences.en: There's an acute threat, which is as this dust gets kicked up from this exposed lake bed,
sentences.zh: 有一个急性威胁，就是当这些灰尘从暴露的湖床上扬起时，

sentences.en: it can cause really serious breathing problems, especially for those who have chronic conditions like asthma or COPD.
sentences.zh: 它会导致非常严重的呼吸问题，特别是对于那些患有哮喘或慢性阻塞性肺病等慢性疾病的人来说。

sentences.en: But long-term, you have a separate thing, which is some of these heavy metals are carcinogens.
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，还有另一件事，就是其中一些重金属是致癌物质。

sentences.en: And over time, they can start taking cases of cancer in people who are exposed to them.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，它们可能会开始在接触这些物质的人群中引发癌症病例。

sentences.en: And so you've got both an immediate shock as the supply of dust increases, and a long-term
sentences.zh: 所以，随着灰尘供应量的增加，你既会面临直接的冲击，也会面临长期的

sentences.en: problem as rates of serious diseases like cancer could very well increase with perennial exposure to these chemicals in the air.
sentences.zh: 问题，因为如果长期暴露在空气中的这些化学物质中，癌症等严重疾病的发病率很可能会增加。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is crazy.
sentences.zh: 好的，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I mean, the bottom of the lake coming up and effectively poisoning the air.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，湖底暴露出来，实际上是在毒害空气。

sentences.en: This sounds incredibly dangerous and potentially catastrophic, both for people in the state of
sentences.zh: 这听起来极其危险，而且可能造成灾难性后果，无论是对犹他州的人民，

sentences.en: Utah and for wildlife that depends on the lake.
sentences.zh: 还是对依赖这个湖的野生动物来说。

sentences.en: And the remarkable thing is that it's not happening at some point in the distant future.
sentences.zh: 最引人注目的是，这并非发生在遥远的未来。

sentences.en: It's happening now.
sentences.zh: 它现在正在发生。

sentences.en: Not only is it happening now, but we know where it's going, or at least where it could go, because this isn't the first time the situation has come up.
sentences.zh: 不仅现在正在发生，而且我们知道它将走向何方，或者至少知道它可能会走向何方，因为这种情况并非第一次出现。

sentences.en: Not too far west of the Great Salt Lake is another lake in California called Owens Lake, which
sentences.zh: 在大盐湖以西不远处，加利福尼亚州还有另一个湖泊，名叫欧文斯湖，它

sentences.en: went through a very similar situation, not due to climate change, but because the river that feeds the lake was diverted to provide drinking water for Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 经历过非常相似的情况，不是因为气候变化，而是因为注入该湖的河流被改道用于为洛杉矶提供饮用水。

sentences.en: After that happened, Owens Lake dried up, and it became the worst source of dust pollution
sentences.zh: 在那之后，欧文斯湖干涸了，并成为了美国最严重的粉尘污染源，

sentences.en: in the United States, requiring enormous spending in the billions of dollars to try to hold that
sentences.zh: 需要耗费数十亿美元的巨额资金来试图抑制这些

sentences.en: dust down, pretty much killing a community on the shore of that lake, what used to be the
sentences.zh: 粉尘，这几乎摧毁了湖岸边的一个社区，也就是曾经的

sentences.en: shore of that lake, and also providing a really, really stark warning that if you let these lakes dry out, the results are catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 湖岸，同时也提供了一个非常、非常严峻的警告：如果你任由这些湖泊干涸，后果将是灾难性的。

sentences.en: Now, what's different is the Great Salt Lake is many times bigger than Owens Lake used to be, number one.
sentences.zh: 现在，不同之处在于，首先，大盐湖的面积比曾经的欧文斯湖大得多。

sentences.en: Number two, it's right next to one of the great Western American cities, Salt Lake City.
sentences.zh: 其次，它紧邻美国西部的一座大城市——盐湖城。

sentences.en: And so, if what happened in the Great Salt Lake were similar to what happened with Owens Lake, the consequences are almost too severe to imagine.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果大盐湖发生的情况与欧文斯湖类似，其后果几乎严重到无法想象。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜店用黑胶唱片做DJ的年代，你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，你会把DJ台变成一个，就像是，

sentences.zh: 充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面陈列着精美的50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能让你免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，免费获取30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Chris, you've just painted a pretty dire picture of Utah's future, if things keep going the way that they're going.
sentences.zh: 那么，克里斯，如果事情继续这样发展下去，你刚刚描绘了一幅犹他州未来的惨淡景象。

sentences.en: I mean, you said it will put two-thirds of the state's population in pretty immediate risk.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你说这会让该州三分之二的人口陷入相当直接的风险之中。

sentences.en: How much do local officials understand the severity of this?
sentences.zh: 当地官员对这一问题的严重性了解多少？

sentences.en: And what are they doing about it?
sentences.zh: 他们对此又在做些什么？

sentences.en: Well, there's no question that state and local officials are aware of the problem.
sentences.zh: 嗯，毫无疑问，州和地方官员都意识到了这个问题。

sentences.en: In this year's state legislative session, state lawmakers really aggressively focused on the problem of the Great Salt Lake and passed a series of bills that are designed to begin
sentences.zh: 在今年的州立法会议上，州议员们非常积极地关注大盐湖的问题，并通过了一系列旨在开始

sentences.en: to address the problem.
sentences.zh: 解决这一问题的法案。

sentences.en: Things like beginning to make it easier to trade water rights or sell water rights to their highest
sentences.zh: 比如开始简化水权交易或将水权出售给其最高

sentences.en: best use, compelling local governments to account for water needs in planning, trying to put some
sentences.zh: 最佳用途，强制地方政府在规划中考虑用水需求，试图对建筑商施加一些

sentences.en: pressure on builders to account for how they use water and things like appliances and homes.
sentences.zh: 压力，要求他们考虑在电器和住宅等方面如何使用水资源。

sentences.en: But none of the laws that were passed in this year's sessions by themselves will really be enough to address this problem.
sentences.zh: 但今年会议通过的法律，单凭任何一项都无法真正足以解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So, for the moment, the actors that matter the most here are local officials, in particular local officials who have authority over drinking water.
sentences.zh: 因此，目前这里最重要的参与者是地方官员，特别是那些对饮用水拥有管辖权的地方官员。

sentences.en: So, back when Salt Lake City was initially being settled by the pioneers and Mormon pioneers in 1847, there is a problem of actually getting this water to upper elevations.
sentences.zh: 所以，早在1847年先驱者和摩门教先驱最初定居盐湖城时，就存在如何将水输送到高海拔地区的问题。

sentences.en: So, when I was in Salt Lake City, I spent time with a woman named Laura Briefer, who was the official
sentences.zh: 所以，当我在盐湖城时，我和一位名叫劳拉·布里弗的女士待在一起，她是

sentences.en: who was in charge of the department that runs that city's drinking water supply.
sentences.zh: 负责运营该市饮用水供应部门的官员。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so the topography wasn't suitable, but then the water...
sentences.zh: 是的，地形不合适，但后来水……

sentences.en: And one of the main points she made was, at some fundamental level, the question of water is not a new problem in Salt Lake City.
sentences.zh: 她提出的主要观点之一是，从根本上讲，水的问题在盐湖城并不是一个新问题。

sentences.en: This is a city built in the desert.
sentences.zh: 这是一座建在沙漠里的城市。

sentences.en: It's always had to worry about its water.
sentences.zh: 它一直不得不为水的问题担忧。

sentences.en: And so, the waters that were more pristine and also could be gravity-fed to a culinary drinking water system were tapped, and those are these mountain streaMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些更纯净且可以通过重力输送到烹饪饮用水系统的水源被开发利用了，这就是那些山间溪流。

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好的，好的。

sentences.en: So, from its earliest days, it sounds like the city has been diverting water from the lake.
sentences.zh: 所以，听起来从建城之初，这座城市就一直在从湖中引水。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess it seemed reasonable in the 19th century, but it turned out to be pretty bad environmental hygiene.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想在19世纪这似乎是合理的，但结果证明这是一种相当糟糕的环境卫生习惯。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The thing to remember is, for a long time, this made sense.
sentences.zh: 要记住的是，在很长一段时间里，这样做是有道理的。

sentences.en: And the things that have changed are relatively new.
sentences.zh: 而发生变化的事情是相对较新的。

sentences.en: The huge population growth and the pressure on that system from drought and heat.
sentences.zh: 巨大的人口增长以及干旱和高温对该系统造成的压力。

sentences.en: So, it turns out there's an upper limit on how many households and businesses you can safely supply water to in Salt Lake City if you don't want the lake to disappear.
sentences.zh: 所以事实证明，如果你不想让湖泊消失，盐湖城能够安全供水的家庭和企业数量是有上限的。

sentences.en: And Laura Briefer drove me around to help me understand how their water system works.
sentences.zh: 劳拉·布里弗带我四处参观，帮助我了解他们的供水系统是如何运作的。

sentences.en: And so, the other source, the reservoir, feeds directly into the plant?
sentences.zh: 所以，另一个水源，即水库，是直接供应到工厂的吗？

sentences.en: Or it's, okay, that sounds nice.
sentences.zh: 或者，好吧，听起来不错。

sentences.en: Okay, so, Laura Briefer's agency, the City Utility Agency, is the government body that keeps an eye on this issue.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以劳拉·布里弗的机构，即城市公用事业局，是负责监督这个问题的政府机构。

sentences.en: But how closely are they following it?
sentences.zh: 但他们跟进得有多紧密呢？

sentences.en: Well, they're following it very closely.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们跟进得非常紧密。

sentences.en: And in fact, they prepare crisis management documents regarding water usage and availability that looks forward decades.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们准备了关于用水和可用性的危机管理文件，展望未来几十年。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And running out of water in this context means that your main supply goes dry and then your reservoir goes dry?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，水用完了意味着你的主要供应干涸了，然后你的水库也干涸了？

sentences.en: Or does it just, maybe the meaning is more simple than just, you don't have the daily supply to meet your daily demand?
sentences.zh: 还是说，也许其含义比单纯的“你没有足够的日常供应来满足日常需求”更简单？

sentences.en: That's daily supply meaning daily demand.
sentences.zh: 那就是日常供应意味着日常需求。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: What do your office's protocols call for?
sentences.zh: 你们办公室的规程要求怎么做？

sentences.en: What would your first step be if demand exceeded supply one day?
sentences.zh: 如果有一天需求超过了供应，你们的第一步会是什么？

sentences.en: And they have different stages indicating how bad the situation is and what to do about it.
sentences.zh: 他们有不同的阶段来表明情况有多糟糕以及该怎么做。

sentences.en: So, we have a water shortage contingency plan.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们有一个缺水应急计划。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there are five stages of action to be taken.
sentences.zh: 有五个阶段的行动需要采取。

sentences.en: And those stages go from stage one, which is sort of a minor shortage, where they advise voluntary reductions in water use, all the way to stage five, which is the most critical
sentences.zh: 这些阶段从第一阶段开始，这是一种轻微的短缺，他们建议自愿减少用水，一直到第五阶段，这是最关键的

sentences.en: stage.
sentences.zh: 阶段。

sentences.en: And you hit the second stage last year?
sentences.zh: 你们去年达到了第二阶段？

sentences.en: We hit the second stage last year, which is a precautionary, very proactive stage.
sentences.zh: 我们去年达到了第二阶段，这是一个预防性的、非常主动的阶段。

sentences.en: Stage two out of five.
sentences.zh: 五个阶段中的第二阶段。

sentences.en: But what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 但那意味着什么？

sentences.en: So, stage two is when you move past strictly voluntary limits and you start to impose mandatory limits on some of the bigger water uses, but not yet on households.
sentences.zh: 所以，第二阶段是指你超越了严格的自愿限制，开始对一些较大的用水户实施强制限制，但尚未针对家庭。

sentences.en: So, it's sort of creeping into the territory of telling people how much water they can use.
sentences.zh: 所以，这有点开始进入告诉人们可以使用多少水的领域了。

sentences.en: I would never want to be in the situation where we ran out of water.
sentences.zh: 我绝不想处于我们水用完的那种境地。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I assume all those stages are designed to prevent that from happening.
sentences.zh: 我假设所有这些阶段都是为了防止这种情况发生而设计的。

sentences.en: So, if you hit stage five, does that mean that your demand has extravagant supply?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你达到了第五阶段，那是否意味着你的需求已经超过了供应？

sentences.en: Or it's the last step that you have to prevent that from happening?
sentences.zh: 还是说这是你为了防止这种情况发生而必须采取的最后一步？

sentences.en: It's the last step we have.
sentences.zh: 这是我们最后的手段。

sentences.en: And in that stage, you know, we ration water.
sentences.zh: 在那个阶段，你知道，我们实行配给用水。

sentences.en: Outdoor irrigation, you know, is very, very limited.
sentences.zh: 户外灌溉，你知道，是非常、非常有限的。

sentences.en: There are mandatory actions that the community has to take and they're regulated.
sentences.zh: 社区必须采取强制性行动，并且这些行动受到监管。

sentences.en: So, at stage five, not only is the city actively policing individual water use, but it also has
sentences.zh: 所以，在第五阶段，城市不仅在积极监管个人的用水，而且还

sentences.en: to go out and try and find ways to bring water in from nearby communities because it can no longer meet its own needs.
sentences.zh: 必须走出去，设法从附近的社区调水，因为它已经无法满足自身的需求了。

sentences.en: But what happens if you actually have demand that exceeds supply and you've gone through five stages?
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的出现了需求超过供应的情况，并且已经经历了五个阶段，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, we've never been there.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们从未到过那种地步。

sentences.en: But for us, we have some interconnected systems with Jordan Valley Water Conservancy District and Central Utah Project.
sentences.zh: 但对我们来说，我们与乔丹谷水利区和犹他州中部项目有一些互联系统。

sentences.en: So, you could draw from neighbors?
sentences.zh: 所以你可以从邻居那里调水？

sentences.en: We could potentially draw from neighbors.
sentences.zh: 我们有可能从邻居那里调水。

sentences.en: One problem with that staging plan is Salt Lake City and the surrounding cities and counties ultimately share the same source of water.
sentences.zh: 那个分阶段计划的一个问题是，盐湖城及其周边的城市和县最终共享同一个水源。

sentences.en: So, if one place runs out, chances are good that the surrounding areas could be running out too.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果一个地方用完了，很有可能周边地区也快用完了。

sentences.en: I hate to be Debbie Downer, but it seems like since it's all one watershed, it's at least plausible that if you ran out of water, your neighbors would as well.
sentences.zh: 我不想当扫兴的人，但既然这都是同一个流域，至少可以想象，如果你没水了，你的邻居可能也会没水。

sentences.en: Hopefully, it doesn't happen that abruptly.
sentences.zh: 希望这种情况不会发生得那么突然。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, hopefully, we see it coming.
sentences.zh: 所以，希望我们能预见到这一点。

sentences.en: So, officials hope that they'll have time to prepare, but the underlying problem is population growth and the population is growing now.
sentences.zh: 所以，官员们希望他们有时间准备，但根本问题是人口增长，而且人口现在正在增长。

sentences.en: And from my reporting and talking to local and state officials, it didn't seem like there was any appetite to do anything that would curb that growth now.
sentences.zh: 根据我的报道以及与地方和州官员的交谈，似乎没有任何意愿去采取任何措施来遏制这种增长。

sentences.en: I read the state water plan that came up in December on my flight in.
sentences.zh: 我在飞来的航班上读了12月份出台的州水资源计划。

sentences.en: One of the things that seemed striking was it seemed to accept as given the premise that the population of the state will double by 2060.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊的一点是，它似乎默认了该州人口到2060年将翻一番的前提。

sentences.en: Not that I'm taking a stance on the wisdom of that, but I thought that seems not to be fixed, right?
sentences.zh: 并不是说我对这种做法的明智性持立场，但我认为这似乎不是不可改变的，对吧？

sentences.en: And it seems like of the universe of potential options, I would have thought that one option might be, well, maybe the state shouldn't grow as much.
sentences.zh: 而且在所有潜在选项中，我原以为其中一个选项可能是，嗯，也许该州不应该增长那么多。

sentences.en: If the question is, how do you find new water supplies for a doubled population?
sentences.zh: 如果问题是，你如何为翻倍的人口寻找新的水源？

sentences.en: Maybe the answer is, don't double your population.
sentences.zh: 也许答案是，不要让人口翻倍。

sentences.en: Do you feel that your office has sort of the pull to say to the development people,
sentences.zh: 你觉得你们办公室是否有某种影响力去对开发商说，

sentences.en: you know, guys, rather than just asking us to find more water, maybe we can ask you to grow less?
sentences.zh: 你知道，伙计们，与其只是要求我们寻找更多的水，也许我们可以要求你们减少增长？

sentences.en: Yeah, that, I don't feel like that is the conversation that happens between water managers and developers very often.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得这并不是水资源管理者和开发商之间经常进行的对话。

sentences.en: But I'm curious, Chris, can someone like Laura Briefer just go to the city and tell them we need to stop growing or we're not going to sustain this?
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，克里斯，像劳拉·布里弗这样的人可以直接去市政府告诉他们我们需要停止增长，否则我们将无法维持下去吗？

sentences.en: So the authority is there in theory.
sentences.zh: 所以理论上是有这种权力的。

sentences.en: But if I want to densify a given plot, do I have to get a permit from your office?
sentences.zh: 但如果我想增加某块土地的密度，我必须从你们办公室获得许可吗？

sentences.en: Yes, we do, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们确实需要，是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And do you use that authority?
sentences.zh: 你们会行使这种权力吗？

sentences.en: Not very often.
sentences.zh: 不经常。

sentences.en: I would think rarely.
sentences.zh: 我想很少。

sentences.en: That would seem like a real buzzkill, politically.
sentences.zh: 从政治上讲，那看起来会非常扫兴。

sentences.en: But the issue, unsurprisingly, is the politics aren't that great.
sentences.zh: 但不出所料，问题在于政治环境并不那么理想。

sentences.en: And of course, there's always politics involved, too.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中也总是涉及政治因素。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so there's a balance that we try to maintain.
sentences.zh: 所以我们试图保持一种平衡。

sentences.en: But your office...
sentences.zh: 但你们办公室……

sentences.en: The impression I got from speaking with Laura Briefer was that she doesn't see it as her job to regulate or affect the rate of growth.
sentences.zh: 我与劳拉·布里弗交谈后得到的印象是，她并不认为监管或影响增长速度是她的工作。

sentences.en: And probably others don't see it as her job either, either at the state or local level.
sentences.zh: 而且可能其他人也不认为这是她的工作，无论是在州还是地方层面。

sentences.en: Those are higher decisions that really, really belong to elected officials.
sentences.zh: 那些是更高级别的决策，真正属于民选官员。

sentences.en: So this is a really hard problem.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常棘手的问题。

sentences.en: And it's the reason we're kind of stuck in a lot of the country in terms of dealing with climate change.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们在处理气候变化方面在全国许多地方陷入困境的原因。

sentences.en: I mean, most places are looking to grow.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大多数地方都寻求增长。

sentences.en: It's equated with progress, right?
sentences.zh: 这等同于进步，对吧？

sentences.en: And a city like Salt Lake City doesn't want to pump the brakes on that, even if the lake is going to dry up.
sentences.zh: 像盐湖城这样的城市不想踩刹车，即使湖泊即将干涸。

sentences.en: Because it would mean saying no to something that everybody wants to say yes to, growth.
sentences.zh: 因为这意味着要对每个人都想说“是”的事情——增长——说“不”。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And it's not just that we want to say yes to growth.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是我们想对增长说“是”。

sentences.en: We want to say yes to low-cost growth, right?
sentences.zh: 我们想对低成本的增长说“是”，对吧？

sentences.en: I think elected officials don't want to impose costs on their constituents.
sentences.zh: 我认为民选官员不想把成本强加给他们的选民。

sentences.en: And they also don't want to say anything about limiting their constituents' choices for how they live.
sentences.zh: 他们也不想对限制选民的生活方式选择发表任何意见。

sentences.en: So if you get a lawn and you want to water that lawn, nobody wants to tell you not to water that lawn.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一片草坪，你想浇灌那片草坪，没人想告诉你不要浇灌那片草坪。

sentences.en: No one wants to tell you where you can or cannot live.
sentences.zh: 没人想告诉你可以在哪里生活，或者不能在哪里生活。

sentences.en: I think there's a mentality in this country that we don't want to impose sacrifice on Americans.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这个国家有一种心态，即我们不想强迫美国人做出牺牲。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, a lot of adapting to climate change really means imposing some degree of sacrifice, some narrowing of the choices that they have.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，适应气候变化的很大一部分确实意味着要做出一定程度的牺牲，缩小他们所拥有的选择范围。

sentences.en: And what's so revealing about this case is Salt Lake City is reluctant to impose meaningful change
sentences.zh: 而这个案例最发人深省的地方在于，盐湖城不愿对其居民强加有意义的改变

sentences.en: or meaningful sacrifice on its residents, even knowing that the cost of inaction could mean poisoning the air and losing their water.
sentences.zh: 或有意义的牺牲，即使明知不作为的代价可能意味着空气中毒和失去水源。

sentences.en: So Chris, if you had to guess and kind of look into your crystal ball,
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯，如果你必须猜测并透过你的水晶球看一看，

sentences.en: what do you think the chances are that the Great Salt Lake will dry up entirely?
sentences.zh: 你认为大盐湖完全干涸的可能性有多大？

sentences.en: I think that's the right question.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是正确的问题。

sentences.en: And it's the same question that I pose to state and local officials when I was in Utah.
sentences.zh: 而且这和我当初在犹他州时向州和地方官员提出的问题是一样的。

sentences.en: And they all told me that they think they'll find a way.
sentences.zh: 他们都告诉我，他们认为自己会找到解决办法。

sentences.en: There's so much that Utah could do.
sentences.zh: 犹他州能做的事情还有很多。

sentences.en: There's so much that Salt Lake City could do.
sentences.zh: 盐湖城能做的事情也还有很多。

sentences.en: They could impose higher costs on water users per gallon and that way get people to do less of the activities that consume lots of water, like water in their lawns.
sentences.zh: 他们可以提高用水户每加仑水的成本，这样就能促使人们减少那些耗水量大的活动，比如给草坪浇水。

sentences.en: They could become a little more aggressive about when they approve and when they deny permits for more construction.
sentences.zh: 在批准和拒绝新的建筑许可时，他们可以采取更积极的态度。

sentences.en: They could be upfront with people about the cost of growing and using water.
sentences.zh: 他们可以坦诚地告诉人们开发和使用水资源的成本。

sentences.en: So there's a lot that could happen.
sentences.zh: 所以，还有很多事情是可以做的。

sentences.en: It's not like it's some binary on-off switch where either they go with the flow or they become environmental radicals, right?
sentences.zh: 这并不是一个非黑即白的开关，要么顺其自然，要么变成激进的环保主义者，对吧？

sentences.en: And so I wouldn't want people to come away from this with the impression that the only salvation for Salt Lake City is doing the unthinkable and slamming the brakes on growth.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想让人们从中得出这样的印象，即盐湖城唯一的救赎就是做那些不可想象的事，强行给经济增长踩刹车。

sentences.en: You could do a lot in the meantime, and it's just not clear to me that even those sort of intermediate fixes are underway because, again, they're not popular.
sentences.zh: 在此期间你可以做很多事情，但我不确定这些中间方案是否正在实施，因为它们同样不受欢迎。

sentences.en: And that just seems to me the most shocking takeaway from all of this.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这才是这一切中最令人震惊的结论。

sentences.en: And Chris, on that note, in the pretty plausible scenario that they don't act fast enough and this dire future you've been describing really does happen,
sentences.zh: 克里斯，说到这一点，在一种很有可能发生的情况下，如果他们行动不够快，而你所描述的那种可怕的未来真的发生了，

sentences.en: what would life in Salt Lake City look like?
sentences.zh: 盐湖城的生活会是什么样子？

sentences.en: I mean, after the story ran, some people joked to me that this is going to be great news for people who make gas masks that filter arsenic out of the air.
sentences.zh: 我是说，报道播出后，有些人跟我开玩笑说，这对那些生产能过滤空气中砷的防毒面具的人来说是个好消息。

sentences.en: And, you know, at some level, you could imagine a world where if everything else fails,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在某种程度上，你可以想象这样一个世界：如果一切都失败了，

sentences.en: living in Salt Lake City becomes an exercise in just expecting the worst, having a gas mask on you in case there's a dust storm, and just accepting it as the cost of living there.
sentences.zh: 住在盐湖城就变成了一种练习，即只做最坏的打算，随身带着防毒面具以防沙尘暴，并将其视为在那里生活的代价。

sentences.en: The air is bad, but people just get used to it.
sentences.zh: 空气很糟糕，但人们已经习惯了。

sentences.en: So, Chris, I wonder how we should be thinking about this problem in terms of the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 所以，克里斯，我想知道我们应该如何从全国其他地区的角度来思考这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, here you have a city that's about to experience this slow-motion car crash, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里有一座城市即将经历一场慢动作的车祸，对吧？

sentences.en: In some sense, it's already started.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，它已经开始了。

sentences.en: And the consequences are understood.
sentences.zh: 而且后果是显而易见的。

sentences.en: They're not disputed.
sentences.zh: 这一点毋庸置疑。

sentences.en: And there are clear solutions.
sentences.zh: 而且有明确的解决方案。

sentences.en: But they are politically and economically very costly.
sentences.zh: 但它们在政治和经济上的代价非常高昂。

sentences.en: So I guess my question for you is, do you think that that is the basic approach we'll see across the United States more broadly?
sentences.zh: 所以我猜我想问你的是，你认为这是否就是我们在美国更广泛范围内会看到的基本应对方式？

sentences.en: That we will likely not try to stop the problem from happening, but put all of our resources into making the problem less bad once it does happen, for better or for worse?
sentences.zh: 即我们可能不会试图阻止问题的发生，而是投入所有的资源，在问题发生后尽量减轻其危害，无论好坏？

sentences.en: So, in one sense, the Great Salt Lake saga is about human nature and how the incentives point towards inaction, even in the face of catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种意义上说，大盐湖的传奇是关于人性的，以及激励机制如何导致人们即使面对灾难也倾向于不作为。

sentences.en: But the class-half-full take on what's happening in Utah might be that other cities could look at this and think, well, we don't want to be like them.
sentences.zh: 但对犹他州正在发生的事情持乐观态度的人可能会认为，其他城市可以看看这里，然后想，好吧，我们不想变成那样。

sentences.en: So maybe the lesson here is anticipate these probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的教训也许是：要预见这些问题。

sentences.en: They tend not to come out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 它们往往不是凭空出现的。

sentences.en: And start a conversation early with your residents and your voters about what the local climate crisis is going to look like.
sentences.zh: 尽早与你的居民和选民开始对话，讨论当地的气候危机将会是什么样子。

sentences.en: And try to figure out some kind of consensus about what people are willing to give up to head off that crisis.
sentences.zh: 并尝试就人们愿意放弃什么来预防这场危机达成某种共识。

sentences.en: I think many cities will look at Utah and say, thank God we don't face those kinds of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我想许多城市会看着犹他州说，谢天谢地，我们没有面临那种问题。

sentences.en: But the reality is almost everywhere in the United States faces some version, some variety of this kind of challenge.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，美国几乎每个地方都面临着某种形式、某种程度的此类挑战。

sentences.en: And the question for all of them is going to be, will you wait as long as Utah did, or will you act faster?
sentences.zh: 而对他们所有人来说，问题在于：你会像犹他州那样等待那么久，还是会行动得更快？

sentences.en: Chris, thank you.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的消息。

sentences.en: Here's what will be clear by the end of this hearing.
sentences.zh: 听证会结束时，以下事实将会变得清晰。

sentences.en: President Trump did not fail to act during the 187 minutes between leaving the Ellipse and telling the mob to go home.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统在离开椭圆形办公室到告诉暴徒回家之间的187分钟里，并非没有采取行动。

sentences.en: He chose not to act.
sentences.zh: 他是选择不采取行动。

sentences.en: During the eighth televised hearing of the January 6th committee, former White House aides recalled that for nearly three hours,
sentences.zh: 在1月6日委员会的第八场电视听证会上，前白宫助手们回忆说，在近三个小时的时间里，

sentences.en: Donald Trump refused to take any steps to call off the rioters or to protect those inside the Capitol, despite their repeated pleas that he do so.
sentences.zh: 尽管助手们一再恳求，唐纳德·特朗普仍拒绝采取任何措施来制止暴徒或保护国会大厦内的人员。

sentences.en: So are you aware of any phone call by the President of the United States to the Secretary of Defense that day?
sentences.zh: 那么，你知道那天美国总统给国防部长打过任何电话吗？

sentences.en: Not that I'm aware of, no.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，没有。

sentences.en: Are you aware of any phone call by the President of the United States to the Attorney General of the United States that day?
sentences.zh: 你知道那天美国总统给美国司法部长打过任何电话吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Are you aware of any phone call by the President of the United States to the Secretary of Homeland Security that day?
sentences.zh: 你知道那天美国总统给国土安全部长打过任何电话吗？

sentences.en: Instead, they said, Trump watched the attack unfold on TV, even as Secret Service agents protecting Vice President Pence at the Capitol became so fearful for their lives
sentences.zh: 相反，他们说，特朗普在电视上看着袭击发生，甚至当在国会大厦保护副总统彭斯的特勤局特工对自己的生命感到如此恐惧时，

sentences.en: that they used their radios to say goodbye to their families.
sentences.zh: 他们通过无线电向家人告别。

sentences.en: Never-before-seen video revealed that when Trump finally did call for rioters to go home on January 6th, he ignored the carefully worded script approved by his aides
sentences.zh: 从未公开的视频显示，当特朗普最终在1月6日呼吁暴徒回家时，他无视了助手们精心准备的讲稿，

sentences.en: and instead sympathized with the rioters in improvised remarks.
sentences.zh: 而是在即兴发言中对暴徒表示了同情。

sentences.en: And then, in a speech the next day, he refused to say that the election was over.
sentences.zh: 然后在第二天的一次演讲中，他拒绝承认选举已经结束。

sentences.en: I'm going to do this.
sentences.zh: 我要这么做。

sentences.en: I'm going to do this.
sentences.zh: 我要这么做。

sentences.en: Let's go.
sentences.zh: 我们走吧。

sentences.en: But this election is now over.
sentences.zh: 但这次选举现在已经结束了。

sentences.en: Congress has certified the results.
sentences.zh: 国会已经认证了结果。

sentences.en: I don't want to say the election's over.
sentences.zh: 我不想说选举结束了。

sentences.en: I just want to say Congress has certified the results without saying the election's over, OK?
sentences.zh: 我只想说国会已经认证了结果，而不说选举结束了，好吗？

sentences.en: And
sentences.zh: 还有

sentences.en: Hey, folks, guess you heard.
sentences.zh: 嘿，伙计们，我想你们听说了。

sentences.en: This morning I tested positive for COVID.
sentences.zh: 今天早上我的新冠检测呈阳性。

sentences.en: But I've been double vaccinated, double boosted.
sentences.zh: 但我已经接种了两剂疫苗，并打了两针加强针。

sentences.en: The symptoms are mild.
sentences.zh: 症状很轻微。

sentences.en: President Biden will isolate in his White House residence for at least five days after testing positive for COVID-19, becoming the second U.S.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统在新冠检测呈阳性后，将在白宫住所隔离至少五天，成为第二位感染该病毒的美国总统。

sentences.en: president to be infected with the virus.
sentences.zh: 总统。

sentences.en: I'm doing well.
sentences.zh: 我感觉很好。

sentences.en: I'm getting a lot of work done.
sentences.zh: 我完成了很多工作。

sentences.en: I'm going to continue to get it done.
sentences.zh: 我将继续完成工作。

sentences.en: The president's physician, Dr. Kevin O'Connor, said that Biden is experiencing fatigue, a runny nose, and a dry cough,
sentences.zh: 总统的私人医生凯文·奥康纳博士说，拜登出现了疲劳、流鼻涕和干咳的症状，

sentences.en: and is taking the antiviral drug Paxlovid to minimize the severity of his infection.
sentences.zh: 并且正在服用抗病毒药物Paxlovid以减轻感染的严重程度。

sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？
